question: How many Falcon 9 or Falcon Heavy orbital launches will SpaceX have in the second half of October 2026?

calls.reasoning: In late Aug 2026 SpaceX ended Falcon 9 Starlink launches from Florida. Since then Falcon cadence has dropped to about 7 a month: September had 7 launches (6 from Vandenberg, 1 from Florida) and October 1-12 had 3. That is about 0.23-0.25 launches a day, or roughly 3.5-4 expected in the 16-day window. Nothing is firmly scheduled inside Oct 16-31 yet: Starlink 15-25 (Oct 12-13), CRS-35 (Oct 13) and USSF-481 (Oct 15 23:44 UTC) all fall just before it, and USSF-481 enters the window if it slips. Bandwagon-5 is listed only as October TBD, and the Vandenberg pad looks capped at about one launch every 4-5 days. No human market was found (the Manifold candidates are unrelated contracts).
calls.dossier:
- Aug 25 2026 (mynews13, aerospaceglobalnews): SpaceX ended Falcon 9 Starlink launches from Florida. Starlink moves to Vandenberg, and Florida Starlink will later fly on Starship (first Florida Starship flight expected early 2027). Other Falcon 9/FH missions continue from Florida.
- Spaceflight Now, Aug 24 2026: the Cape workforce has been refocused on Starship. At that point 2026 had 76 Starlink missions, 44 of them from Vandenberg.
- Earlier 2026 pace: 50th Falcon 9 launch on Apr 26 and about 68 by mid-June (Spaceflight Now), i.e. about 0.38-0.43 per day.
- Spaceflight Now, Sep 25 2026: September had 6 Falcon 9 launches from Vandenberg and just 1 from the East Coast, 7 in total.
- Vandenberg Starlink missions were spaced out: 80th Starlink of 2026 on Sep 5, 81st (15-27) on Sep 19, then Starlink 15-25 delayed from Sep 30, Oct 10 and Oct 11 to NET Oct 12 23:00 UTC.
- October launches so far (Wikipedia list Oct-Dec 2026): Crew-13 on Oct 1 (Florida), Transporter-18 on Oct 1 (Vandenberg), SDA T1TL-A on Oct 10 07:39 UTC (Vandenberg; aborted Oct 5, then delays).
- Schedule as of Oct 12 (nextspaceflight, rocketlaunch.org, SFN): Starlink 15-25 Oct 12-13 (VSFB), CRS-35 Oct 13 10:33 UTC (CCSFS), USSF-481 Oct 15 23:44 UTC (VSFB). No dated Falcon launches listed for Oct 16-31. Bandwagon-5 (CCSFS) is listed only as October TBD. Next SDA Tranche 1 date not announced. No Falcon Heavy is scheduled in the window.
- USSF-481 is set 16 minutes before the window opens, so any slip puts it inside the window.
- Status quo: the post-August regime of about 7 Falcon launches a month, dominated by the single Vandenberg pad SLC-4E.
- Base rates: Sep 2026 had 7 launches in 30 days (about 3.7 per 16 days); Oct 1-12 had 3 in 12 days. The pre-August 2026 pace (about 6-7 per 16 days) applies only to the old regime that included Florida Starlink.
- Resolves off Wikipedia's 'List of Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy launches', UTC dates, inclusive.
- Event window: Oct 16 00:00 -> Oct 31 23:59 UTC 2026. As of Oct 12 09:01 UTC, 0% has elapsed.
- Searched but not found: firm dates for any Falcon launch Oct 16-31, the cadence of Vandenberg Starlink missions after Oct 12, any market on this question.
calls.reference_class: Falcon launches per 16-day window in the post-Aug-2026 regime (no Florida Starlink): Sept 2026 had 7 in 30 days, Oct 1-12 had 3

calls.reasoning: Reference class: SpaceX Falcon launches per 16-day window. In 2025 that was ~7, but by late 2026 the pace has fallen because the Cape Canaveral workforce moved to Starship. Falcon 9 hit 100 launches on Aug 24 and ~108 by late Sept (~8 per month). September had 7 launches (6 Vandenberg, 1 Cape). October 1-15 has about 6, counting the scheduled ones. No launches are dated inside Oct 16-31 yet; Bandwagon-5 is listed only as NET October. Vandenberg SLC-4E at ~6-7 per month gives ~3-3.5 in the window, plus occasional Cape customer missions, so the mean is ~3.5-4. Upside if USSF-481 slips into Oct 16 UTC; downside from scrubs. No human market found; the Manifold candidates (Blue Moon on Falcon Heavy, Falcon reaching 800 launches) do not match this contract.

calls.reasoning: Post-Aug-2026 regime (Falcon 9 Starlink ended at the Cape, Vandenberg SLC-4E dominant): ~7-8 Falcon launches/month, ~0.25/day, so the mean is ~3.7-4 in the 16-day window. Nothing firmly dated in Oct 16-31. Bandwagon-5 is NET October; USSF-481 at Oct 15 23:44Z enters the window on any slip; Vandenberg Starlink spacing is lengthening. Pad cadence makes the count less dispersed than Poisson, but the possible wind-down of Falcon Starlink keeps real mass at two or fewer. No human market found (Manifold candidates unrelated).
calls.reconciliation: All runs agree on the regime shift and a rate of ~0.23-0.25/day. Factual disputes: (1) Run 2's early-October Falcon Heavy NRO launch: unverifiable without web access, and outside the window either way, so it does not matter. (2) Exact launch counts for September and October so far: consistent enough across dossiers (Sep = 7). The rest is judgment on tail weight. I anchored on a Poisson with mean 3.8, narrowed it for pad-cadence regularity, kept a heavier low tail for the Starlink wind-down and the lack of dated missions, and kept some upside for a USSF-481 slip.
